verses.text: Follow my example, just as I follow Christ’s.
Family, I appreciate that you remember me in everything and hold on to the teachings I passed to you.
But I want you to understand this: Christ is the head of every man, the man is the head of the woman, and God is the head of Christ.
When a man prays or speaks God’s message with his head covered, he dishonors his head.
But when a woman prays or speaks God’s message with her head uncovered, she dishonors her head. It’s like she shaved it.
If a woman won’t cover her head, she might as well cut her hair off too. But if short or shaved hair brings her shame, she should cover her head.
A man shouldn’t cover his head, since he is God’s image and glory; but woman is man’s glory.
Man didn’t come from woman; woman came from man.
Man wasn’t created for woman; woman was created for man.
That’s why a woman should have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
Still, in the Lord, neither woman nor man is independent of the other.
Yes, woman came from man, but every man comes through a woman—and everything comes from God.
Judge this for yourselves: does it look right for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
Doesn’t nature itself show that long hair dishonors a man?
But long hair is a woman’s glory; her hair was given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we don’t have that custom, and neither do God’s churches.
Here’s one thing I can’t praise you for: when you meet, you’re making things worse, not better.
First, I hear that when you gather as a church, there are divisions among you—and I can believe it.
Some factions are bound to show up, so it becomes clear who’s truly approved.
When you all gather, it isn’t really the Lord’s Supper you’re eating.
Each person rushes ahead with their own meal. One goes hungry, another gets drunk.
Don’t you have homes to eat and drink in? Or are you looking down on God’s church and shaming people who have nothing? What should I say—good job? I can’t praise you for this.
This is what I received from the Lord and passed on to you: on the night Jesus was betrayed, he took bread.
After giving thanks, he broke it and said, “Take this and eat it. This is my body, given for you. Keep doing this to remember me.”
In the same way, after supper he took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me.”
Every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord’s death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way that dishonors him is guilty of sinning against the Lord’s body and blood.
First, each person should check themselves. Then they can eat the bread and drink from the cup.
Anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the Lord’s body brings judgment on themselves.
That’s why many of you are weak and sick, and some have even died.
If we checked ourselves honestly, we wouldn’t come under judgment.
But when the Lord judges us, he’s correcting us so we won’t be condemned along with the world.
So, family, when you gather to eat, wait for one another.
If someone’s hungry, eat at home first. Then when you gather, it won’t bring judgment. I’ll take care of the other matters when I come.
